summary: The root ت ب ب primarily signifies perishing, being ruined, or suffering loss. It implies a state of destruction, failure, or being cut off from good.

headwords.def: تَبڤبَ [ تَبَّ , aor. تَبِبَ , inf. n. تَبٌّ , and perhaps and and , He, or it, suffered loss, or diminution; or became lost: and perished, or died: as also , inf. n. تَتْبِيبٌ : and app. تُبَّ also.] تَبٌّ (M, A, K) and (M, K) [as inf. ns.] signify The suffering loss, or diminution; or being lost: and perishing, or dying: or [used as substs.] loss, or diminution; or the state of being lost: and perdition, or death: (M, * A, K: *) and so , (T, S, A, Msb, K,) [said to be] a subst. from تَبَّبَهُ , with teshdeed, (Msb,) and and : (K:) or the last three signify [simply] perdition, or death: (M:) and is explained as signifying loss, or diminution, that brings, or leads, to perdition or death; (IAth, TA;) and so ; (Bd in cxi. 1;) and the causing to perish. (T, TA.) Hence you say,

headwords.def: استتبّ أستتب استتب ٱستتاب ٱستتب (tropical:) It (a road) became beaten, or trodden, and rendered even, or easy to walk or ride upon, or easy and direct. (A.) (tropical:) It (an affair) was, or became, rightly disposed or arranged; in a right state: (S, M, A, Msb:) or it followed a regular, or right, course; was in a right state; and clear, or plain: from مُسْتَتِبٌّ applied to a road, explained below: (T, TA:) or it became complete, and in a right state: lit. it demanded loss, or diminution, or destruction; because these sometimes follow completeness: (Har p. 35:) or the ب may be a substitute for م ; the meaning being استتمّ . headwords.def: تَبُّوبٌ بوب تبوب i. q. مَهْلَكَةٌ [ A place of perdition, or destruction; or a desert; or a desert such as is termed مَفَازَة ]. (K.) headwords.gloss: old; weak; I was a young man, and I have become an old man

parts.t: man; (AZ, T, M, A, K;) fem. with
: of the dial. of Hudheyl; and extr. [with respect to analogy]. (M.) You say,
I was a young man, and I have become an old man
Art thou a young woman or an old woman?

headwords.def: تَابٌّ أبى تأب تاب (tropical:) An old man; (AZ, T, M, A, K;) fem. with ة : (AZ, T, M, A:) and (assumed tropical:) weak: pl. أَتْبَابٌ : of the dial. of Hudheyl; and extr. [with respect to analogy]. (M.) You say, كُنْتُ شَابًّا فَصِرْتُ تَابًّا [ I was a young man, and I have become an old man ]. (A.) And أَشَابَّةٌ أَنْتِ أَمْ تَابَّةٌ [ Art thou a young woman or an old woman? ] (A.) Also, (T, K,) or تَابُّ الظَّهْرِ , (T,) (assumed tropical:) An ass, and a camel, having galls, or sores, on his back: (T, K:) pl. as above. (K.) [See also بَاتٌّ .]

headwords.gloss: Furrowed by passengers, so that it is manifest to him who travels along it

parts.t: Furrowed by passengers, so that it is manifest to him who travels along it;
and to this is likened an affair that is clear, or plain, and in a right state. (T.) [See the verb, 10.]

headwords.def: مُسْتَتِبٌّ مستتب , applied to a road, (tropical:) Furrowed by passengers, so that it is manifest to him who travels along it; and to this is likened an affair that is clear, or plain, and in a right state. (T.) [See the verb, 10.]

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
